questions.q: What does Git integration actually store for a Fabric Notebook?
options: The source code itself — the actual %%pyspark or %%sql cells — saved as a plain text file
A binary snapshot of the entire notebook environment
Only the notebook's last-run output table
A screenshot of the notebook's UI
questions.explain: For an Eventstream or KQL Queryset, it's a JSON definition instead — either way, it's human-readable and diffable.

questions.q: Why would committing a notebook's cell output alongside its code create noisy diffs?
options: The output changes every time the underlying data changes, even when the code itself didn't, generating a diff for meaningless changes
Notebook output is always identical to the code and produces no diff
Git cannot store any kind of table output at all
Output and code are stored in completely separate, unrelated systems
questions.explain: Fabric's Git integration tracks the source code of a notebook, not its last-run output, for exactly this reason.

questions.q: Why can a KQL Queryset change be reviewed like a code change in a pull request?
options: Because its definition is a readable JSON file, so a change to it produces a real, understandable diff
KQL changes can never actually be reviewed before merging
KQL Querysets are stored as binary files with no diffable content
Pull requests only work with PySpark code, never KQL
questions.explain: A reviewer can see exactly what changed — like a 5-minute bucket becoming 1-minute — and ask questions before it merges.

questions.q: How does version control relate to CI/CD (Lesson 45)?
options: Version control isn't separate from CI/CD — it's the input CI/CD actually reacts to; every commit on the tracked branch is a potential trigger
They are two completely unrelated systems with no connection
CI/CD replaces the need for version control entirely
Version control only matters after CI/CD has already deployed something
questions.explain: The branch and pull-request workflow puts a human review step in front of that automated trigger.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a pull request in this branching workflow?
options: A human review step that lets a teammate see the diff and ask questions before the change merges and reaches CI/CD
It automatically deploys the change to production immediately
It replaces the need for a dev/test/prod environment split
It only applies to notebook changes, never to KQL or Eventstream changes
questions.explain: This is the review step that sits between a commit and CI/CD's automated build/test/deploy trigger.
